items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:25:1
items.html:
Their main illumination is only through the anterior of Adam Kadmon, yet a little illumination of these Nekudim does expand, etc.: This matter has already been explained at length above (Part 4, page 239, Chapter 5, in the Inner Light, section 2), and from there you should seek it. And the gist is that “sides,” which are the discernment of right and left in a Partzuf, mean this: an abundance of Hassadim is called right, and a paucity of Hassadim is called left. And the place of the reception of Hochma and GAR [first three] is called anterior, and the place that is unfit for the reception of GAR is called posterior. See there. Therefore the Rosh [head] and Toch of every Partzuf down to the Tabur are called anterior, for down to the Tabur it is fit to receive the light of GAR; and the place from the Tabur downwards is called posterior, for it is not fit to receive GAR there. See there.
And you already know of the new restriction that was made through the ascent of MAN [female waters] to the Nikvey Einayim, whereby the AHP of the Rosh came out from there into the discernment of a Guf [body], and the Peh [mouth] became the discernment of the Sium upon the illumination of GAR, in the likeness of the Tabur, for this is why the light of the Ozen was blocked in the Shibolet, as above in the adjacent item. Therefore the illumination of the light of the Einayim is called by the name “anterior,” for they do not illuminate the vessels of the posterior, which are from the Peh downwards, but only a small discernment of illumination by way of the sides, that is, what is extended from the discernment of right and left, whose meaning is the illumination of Hassadim, as above.
